sd_contact_reason.description: Classify the reason someone contacted ScienceDirect support into exactly one of 13 categories. Each category carries a Definition saying when to use it and what not to use it for. Assign the single best-fitting LEAF code (e.g. SDCR5.1). Decide what actually blocked the customer before what they were talking about. If an explicit security or network control denied access — access denied, IP blocked, Cloudflare, firewall, suspected crawling — classify the ticket as 'Access blocked by security/network controls' even when content or signing in is also mentioned. If the obstacle is a failed sign-in, choose between 'Institutional sign in not working' (SSO, SAML, Shibboleth, institution not recognised) and 'Login issues' (an individual account, password, activation or verification link) by asking who owns the credentials. Use 'Accessing content' only when signing in worked and the failure is entitlement, coverage or a paywall. Prefer a specific category over either 'Other' category, and use 'Not enough info' only when the ticket genuinely does not say enough to tell. When money is involved, separate the transaction from the entitlement. If the complaint is about the payment or the order itself — the payment failed or would not go through, a double charge, a missing receipt or confirmation, a refund, an invoice or a price — classify it as 'Other - not access related', whose own signals name invoices and sales. Send complaints about the content itself in the same direction — poor or wrong images, typographical errors, or requests for corrections. Reserve 'Accessing content' for the case where the purchase or subscription is not in dispute but the content still will not open: purchase not recognised means a completed purchase the system fails to honour, not a purchase that failed.
